articles.title: In 2001, an Air Transat jet carrying 306 people ran out of fuel over the Atlantic after a leak; Captain Robert Piche glided the powerless Airbus for about 19 minutes to a runway in the Azores, and everyone survived
articles.summary: A routine transatlantic journey from Canada to Portugal became a fight for survival when an Air Transat passenger jet lost both its engines over the
articles.body: A routine transatlantic journey from Canada to Portugal became a fight for survival when an Air Transat passenger jet lost both its engines over the Atlantic Ocean in August 2001. With no engine power and land still some distance away, Captain Robert Piché and First Officer Dirk DeJager had to guide the aircraft towards an airport in the Azores, relying on the plane's ability to glide. All 306 people aboard survived the emergency landing, although several passengers and crew members were injured. According to the Portuguese aviation accident investigation report, CBC News and the Aviation Safety Network, the Airbus A330 ran out of fuel because of a leak that developed during the flight. The incident, involving Air Transat Flight 236, later became known as the Azores Glider and remains one of the most remarkable examples of an unpowered passenger aircraft landing.The flight departed Toronto Pearson International Airport on August 23, 2001, bound for Lisbon, Portugal, with 293 passengers and 13 crew members aboard. The aircraft, an Airbus A330-243, was just over two years old. It was commanded by Piché, an experienced pilot with more than 16,000 flight hours, alongside first officer DeJager. Around four hours into the journey, a fracture developed in a fuel line connected to the aircraft's right engine. The resulting leak caused fuel to escape at an alarming rate, eventually leaving the aircraft with far less fuel than its instruments and flight plan initially suggested. The crew first noticed unusual oil temperature and pressure readings in the right engine. However, the warnings were not immediately identified as signs of a fuel leak. The pilots contacted the airline's maintenance control centre and were advised to monitor the situation.A subsequent fuel imbalance warning prompted the crew to transfer fuel between the aircraft's tanks. However, the procedure inadvertently sent more fuel towards the leaking engine, accelerating the loss. By the time the pilots recognised the seriousness of the situation, a substantial amount of fuel had already been lost. At 5.45 UTC on August 24, the pilots decided to divert to Lajes Air Base on Terceira Island in the Azores, a Portuguese archipelago in the Atlantic.At 6.13 UTC, the right engine stopped after running out of fuel. The aircraft was still approximately 150 nautical miles from Lajes. The crew continued descending towards the island, but the situation deteriorated further when the left engine also shut down at 6.26 UTC, leaving the aircraft without any engine power. With both engines out, the Airbus became a glider. Its emergency ram air turbine automatically deployed, providing enough electrical and hydraulic power to operate essential flight controls and instruments. However, several other systems, including the normal braking and flap systems, were no longer available.A 19-minute glide towards the runwayThe aircraft was now around 65 nautical miles from Lajes, and the pilots had to make every remaining manoeuvre count. Air traffic controllers at the military airbase used radar to guide the aircraft towards the runway. Piché and DeJager worked together to manage the descent and maintain enough altitude to reach the airport. With the aircraft losing height rapidly, the captain also performed a series of turns to reduce its altitude and line it up for landing.After approximately 19 minutes without engine power, the aircraft reached Lajes Airport at 6.45 UTC on August 24. It touched down on Runway 33 at around 200 knots, considerably faster than a normal landing speed. The landing was hard, and the aircraft bounced once before touching down again. With its antiskid braking system unavailable, the main landing gear wheels locked, causing the tyres to deflate and sustain severe damage as the aircraft travelled along the runway. It eventually came to a stop, using much of the available runway.The emergency evacuation began immediately. All 306 people survived, although 16 passengers and two crew members sustained injuries, including two passengers who were seriously injured but not in a life-threatening condition. The aircraft itself suffered substantial damage to its landing gear and lower fuselage.What caused the aircraft to run out of fuel?An investigation led by Portugal's Aviation Accidents Prevention and Investigation Department, with assistance from the Transportation Safety Board of Canada, examined the circumstances behind the incident. Investigators traced the fuel leak to a maintenance error involving incompatible parts fitted during the replacement of the aircraft's right engine. A hydraulic line had been installed too close to a fuel line, allowing the two to rub against each other during operation. The friction eventually caused a crack in the fuel line, through which fuel escaped.The investigation also identified shortcomings in how the cockpit crew interpreted the fuel warnings and responded to the imbalance. Their decision to follow the fuel imbalance procedure without recognising the possibility of a leak contributed to the loss of fuel. Air Transat accepted responsibility for the maintenance-related failure and was fined C$250,000 by Canadian authorities in September 2001. The accident also prompted changes to aircraft operating procedures and fuel-leak warnings to help prevent similar incidents.Recognition for the flight crewThe successful landing brought international attention to Piché and DeJager. In 2002, Piché received the Air Line Pilots Association's Superior Airmanship Award in recognition of his handling of the emergency. The incident also became the subject of documentaries, aviation programmes and the 2010 Canadian biographical film Piché: The Landing of a Man, which depicts the captain's life and the events surrounding Flight 236.Often remembered as the Azores Glider, the flight remains a landmark in commercial aviation. Its 65-nautical-mile unpowered journey demonstrated the importance of cockpit coordination, emergency decision-making and the ability of flight crews to respond under extraordinary circumstances.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2018, an Omaha apartment complex closed amid code complaints, forcing tenants to move; after reopening in 2021, its owner pursued a lawsuit against the city, but a 2026 appeals ruling rejected the claims
articles.summary: A federal appeals court has rejected all civil rights claims filed by the owner of an Omaha apartment complex against city officials.
articles.body: A federal appeals court has rejected all civil rights claims filed by the owner of an Omaha apartment complex against city officials. The decision upholds the dismissal of a lawsuit that began after the city closed the building over code violations in 2018. The ruling was issued on Friday, 6 November 2026, by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit. It upheld a District of Nebraska decision that dismissed claims brought by AB Realty, LLC, and the property owners, Kay and Janea Anderson. The legal dispute began in 2018 when Omaha city inspectors carried out a search warrant at the Yale Park Apartment Complex. They reported serious health and safety problems that forced tenants to leave the building. After carrying out major repairs, AB Realty reopened the complex in 2021. The company then sued city inspectors Scott Lane and Kevin Mulcahy, housing advocates and the city itself. It claimed that officials had violated its rights under the Fourth, Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments. Writing for the unanimous appeals panel, Circuit Judge L. Steven Kobes said the property owners had failed to prove that officials violated their constitutional rights. He found that the original search warrant was still supported by enough evidence and that the owners had not provided enough legal detail to support their claims about due process and property rights.Ruling on search warrant and probable causeThe main part of AB Realty's appeal challenged the search warrant used for the 2018 inspection under the Fourth Amendment. The property owners argued that city housing inspector Scott Lane included false information in his written request for the warrant. This included claims that officials had asked for permission to enter the building and been refused, that police had been called to the complex, and that a gas leak had caused an explosion. Under a federal legal rule established in Franks v. Delaware, a search warrant can be ruled invalid if an officer knowingly or carelessly includes false information that is needed to show there is enough reason to carry out a search. However, the Eighth Circuit judges ruled that even if the disputed statements were removed, the rest of the warrant application still contained enough evidence of serious building code violations to justify the inspection. "Even excluding the information disputed by AB Realty, the warrant application established probable cause for the inspection warrant," the court stated in its written decision. The court also rejected claims that the city had broken Nebraska inspection laws by failing to ask for voluntary permission to enter before requesting a search warrant. The judges explained that breaking a state procedure does not automatically mean that officials have violated federal constitutional rights under Section 1983.Deficiencies in due process and takings claimsThe Eighth Circuit also rejected AB Realty's claims under the Fourteenth Amendment, which protects due process rights, and the Fifth Amendment, which protects property owners against certain government takings. The property owners claimed that city officials had made several mistakes. These included closing the entire 60-unit complex instead of shutting down only individual apartments, putting up warning signs incorrectly, delaying approval of repairs and making negative comments about the owners to private contractors. The court described these claims as "scattershot allegations". It said the owners had not clearly explained which officials were responsible for each action or exactly which constitutional rights had been violated. "Since AB Realty has failed to identify what constitutionally protected interests are at stake, we cannot assess what process was constitutionally due," the appeals court stated. On the Fifth Amendment claim, the judges pointed out that the City of Omaha had not taken ownership of the land or seized it for public use. This meant there had been no physical taking of the property. The panel also said AB Realty had failed to make its case under the legal rules that apply when government regulations reduce the value or use of private property.Resolution of lower court proceedingsThe Eighth Circuit's decision, issued under docket number 25-2082, brings the federal court case linked to the 2018 closure to an end. The first motions in the case were handled by the late U.S. District Judge Laurie Smith Camp. She partly dismissed the claims and paused the federal case while state criminal charges linked to the building's conditions were being considered against Kay Anderson. After a state trial court found Anderson guilty of some misdemeanor offences, U.S. Chief District Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr. dismissed the remaining federal claims. This led AB Realty to appeal the decision. The appeals panel concluded that without proof of an underlying constitutional violation, neither the city nor its individual officials could be held legally responsible under Section 1983. The decision brings the civil lawsuit to a final close.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Transformers actor Josh Duhamel joins Bobcat company to donate a new utility vehicle to Los Angeles firefighters supporting the city's first full-time paid wildland hand crew
articles.summary: Actor and director Josh Duhamel partnered with Bobcat Company to surprise Los Angeles firefighters with a brand-new Bobcat UV34XL utility vehicle in June
articles.body: Actor and director Josh Duhamel partnered with Bobcat Company to surprise Los Angeles firefighters with a brand-new Bobcat UV34XL utility vehicle in June 2025. The donation was made in recognition of the Los Angeles Fire Department's first full-time, paid wildland hand crew, which helps mitigate and control wildfires. Duhamel personally handed over the keys to the vehicle during a surprise visit to LAFD Station 88 as part of Bobcat's 'Work Worth Doing' campaign. The equipment is intended to support the crew during future wildfire operations, while the company also pledged a portion of proceeds from a limited-edition hat to the Los Angeles Fire Department Foundation.How will Duhamel's Bobcat vehicle donation help Los Angeles firefightersAccording to an official press release by Bobcat, the donation was intended to provide additional equipment for firefighters involved in wildfire mitigation and suppression. Bobcat said the utility vehicle would support the department's first full-time, paid wildland hand crew as it carries out its responsibilities. The company described the vehicle as a practical contribution towards the work of firefighters who help protect communities from wildfires.Speaking about the donation, Duhamel highlighted the importance of supporting emergency responders. "I think this is some of the most honourable work that you can do. It takes a special kind of person to sign up as a firefighter, especially in a place like Los Angeles where wildfires run rampant," he said. He added: "We believe, myself and Bobcat, that the firefighters deserve the best tools out there, and that's why we wanted to donate this machine. I think that anytime you can support those who are protecting others is definitely work worth doing."How will Josh Duhamel's donation help Los Angeles firefightersThe Los Angeles Fire Department welcomed the donation, with Captain and Public Information Officer Adam VanGerpen acknowledging the contribution from Duhamel and Bobcat. He said the equipment would help the department strengthen its wildfire response efforts by improving the efficiency of its hand crew."We are grateful for Bobcat and Josh's commitment to advancing our efforts with the generous donation of a Bobcat UTV," VanGerpen said. He further explained: "This will enhance our hand crew's efficiency in mitigating and fighting wildfires, enabling us to achieve so much more in our mission to keep the community safe."The utility vehicle is intended to be used during future wildfire operations, supporting the crew's work in mitigating and controlling fires. The department's hand crew is the first of its kind in Los Angeles to operate on a full-time, paid basis. The donation therefore forms part of the company's effort to provide equipment to people carrying out essential work in their communities.How is Bobcat extending its support beyond Los Angeles firefightersThe donation to the Los Angeles Fire Department was one of several contributions made through Bobcat's 'Work Worth Doing' initiative in 2025. The company launched the campaign in May by partnering with entrepreneur and Magnolia co-founder Chip Gaines to surprise Jason Shields, a United States veteran and founder of Hoof Haven Sanctuary, with a Bobcat T595 compact track loader.Hoof Haven Sanctuary is a non-profit organisation that rescues endangered or injured horses, provides rehabilitation and finds them permanent homes. Bobcat said the initiative would continue throughout 2025, with other company ambassadors, including country musician Justin Moore and professional BMX rider Ryan Nyquist, visiting and recognising people making a difference in their communities.Alongside the utility vehicle donation, Bobcat also announced additional support for the Los Angeles Fire Department Foundation. articles.title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10
articles.summary: The government says pupils in Year 7 to 9 should have "richer, more engaging" learning than preparing for GCSEs.
articles.body:
Secondary schools will be told not to teach GCSEs early as part of a major shake-up of how children in Years 7 to 9 are taught.

The government plans to make Key Stage 3 a more distinct education phase, urging schools to focus less on exams and more on a "richer, more engaging" experience.

The changes come in response to two reviews that found pupils were increasingly becoming disengaged in their early teenage years, affecting attendance and achievement, the Department for Education (DfE) said.

The move will mark a reversal of the approach taken by the previous Conservative government to focus the first three years of secondary school on core subjects and on doing well in assessments.

Former Education Secretary Michael Gove prioritised English, maths and science, while raising grade boundaries, making exams harder and limiting resits.

He also made GCSEs linear, meaning they are sat all in one go at the end of Year 11 instead of over the course of Key Stage 4.

These reforms meant teachers started preparing pupils for exams at an earlier stage at the expense of teaching unexamined parts of their subject.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell said: "The early years of secondary school should be a time when children are excited to go to school and engage in the specialist and much broader teaching on offer, and where they find their passion and develop a love of learning."

She added that ringfencing Key Stage 3 studies would allow for "more time to develop deeper understanding, as well as a richer experience that will engage more young people in their passions".

The DfE has pledged a "more engaging offer" in subjects like drama, PE, music and languages, which have seen a decline in students taking them, when it publishes its new curriculum later this year.

It says persistent absence nearly doubles among pupils between Year 6 and Year 9, from 13% to 15%.

The department pointed to a recent survey commissioned by the International Baccalaureate that found GCSE prep dominated Key Stage 3 learning in England, with 57% of teachers saying it was the leading influence on the curriculum.

"The pressures of GCSEs and an overcrowded curriculum are resulting in too many children receiving a narrower offer during Key Stage 3 and being rushed towards exams without grasping the fundamentals or developing deeper understanding," Powell said. "I'm putting a stop to that."

A 2015 Ofsted report suggested that Key Stage 3 may be "wasted years", echoing the view at the time that pupils aged 11-14 lacked a clear motivation to work hard.

However, the government faced criticism at the time that its reforms made each exam far more significant, meaning teachers refocused lessons only on what could come up in them.

Reacting to the DfE's announcement on Sunday, Lib Dem education spokeswoman Munira Wilson MP said school was "more than drilling kids for exams" but cautioned against "micromanaging" teachers.

She added that a new curriculum "alone won't get children back into the classroom", noting that "too many pupils are missing school because of anxiety and unmet mental health needs" while "schools can't offer more drama, music and languages without the teachers to teach them".

articles.title: ‘They’re a failing nation’: Trump says fresh Iran strikes ‘highly unlikely’ if Tehran signs ‘strong agreement’
articles.summary: US president Donald Trump has said it is “highly unlikely” that he will order American forces to resume military operations against Iran if Tehran makes
articles.body: US president Donald Trump has said it is “highly unlikely” that he will order American forces to resume military operations against Iran if Tehran makes tangible progress in negotiations over its nuclear programme and the reopening of the strategic Strait of Hormuz.However, he warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if further military action became necessary, CNN reported.In a 20-minute telephone interview with CNN, Trump repeated five times that renewed military intervention was unlikely, provided Iran agreed to what he described as a strong agreement.“It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement,” Trump told CNN. “The answer is highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary.”He also claimed that economic sanctions and previous American military strikes had significantly weakened Iran's capabilities.“They’re a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301% inflation. Highly unlikely it will be necessary. I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don’t know how hard I hit them,” he said.“So it’s highly unlikely I’ll have to. They’re withering away financially. We’ve hit them militarily. We could finish them off,” Trump added.Revealing the extent of potential targets, the US President told CNN: “We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They’ll all be down.”Explaining why he had not ordered the destruction of the infrastructure, Trump said: “I don’t want to do that because essentially, it’ll take 10 years to rebuild them. I don’t like ripping down bridges. And the hardest thing to build is a bridge. It takes years, and I’m a good builder.”Meanwhile, Tehran has dismissed suggestions that political developments in Washington could influence its position towards the US. Mohamed Mokhber, an adviser to Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, urged the government to focus on domestic economic resilience rather than American electoral outcomes, Al Jazeera reported.“It is naive to tie our fate to Washington,” Mokhber wrote on X. “It is necessary to mobilise our economic resources. Time is a national asset; it must not be wasted.”Separately, Brigadier General Shekarchi, spokesperson for Iran's Armed Forces, warned Washington against continuing what Tehran describes as hostile policies towards the Islamic Republic. His remarks were carried by Iranian state broadcaster Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB).“The political and electoral developments in the United States and the successive defeats of the Trump administration and his party colleagues in various fields are, rather than being the result of superficial fluctuations in the country's domestic politics, a reflection of a larger and undeniable reality: defeat against the will of a powerful Iran,” he said.Shekarchi also described Washington's military strategy as ineffective, claiming that its approach had weakened American influence in West Asia.“Any power that lines up against the solid, steadfast rock and the divine and steely will of Islamic Iran will have no end but collapse and disintegration in the world's public opinion,” he added.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Georgia couple spent $40,000 turning the husband's pre-marital home basement into a separate space for her parents; after divorce, an appeals court ordered the property split to be reconsidered
articles.summary: A Georgia divorce dispute over a house renovation has prompted an appeals court to reconsider how a couple's shared investment should be treated when
articles.body: A Georgia divorce dispute over a house renovation has prompted an appeals court to reconsider how a couple's shared investment should be treated when dividing marital property. The husband owned the home before marriage, but the couple later spent approximately $40,000 finishing its basement and creating a separate living area for the wife's parents. When their marriage ended, the house became the central issue in their financial settlement. The Georgia Court of Appeals ruled that the lower court had incorrectly calculated the property's marital value, requiring a fresh division of the couple's assets.$40,000 basement renovation became central to the Georgia divorce caseAccording to the Court of Appeals of Georgia's March 10, 2026, decision in Pelayo v. Pelayo, the couple married in April 2016 and separated in June 2024. Meredith Pelayo filed for divorce on June 11, 2024, while her husband, Allen Pelayo, subsequently filed his own response and counterclaim.The couple had no children together, and the main disagreement during their divorce concerned how their property and financial assets should be divided.Allen had purchased the marital residence before the marriage, making it his individually owned property at the outset. However, the house underwent substantial financial changes during their marriage, including mortgage repayments and renovations funded with money belonging to both spouses.One significant project involved completing the basement and converting it into an independent living space for Meredith's parents. The renovation cost approximately $40,000, according to the court's account of the evidence presented during the divorce trial.The investment became important because it represented money contributed during the marriage to improve a house originally owned by one spouse.How the property's value changed during the marriageThe court's decision outlined the property's financial position at different stages of the relationship.When the couple married, the residence had an appraised value of $286,000 and an outstanding mortgage of $246,000. This meant the house had approximately $40,000 in equity, representing the difference between its value and the remaining loan.By the time of the divorce trial, the property had increased in appraised value to $555,000, and the mortgage balance had decreased to $205,000.Consequently, its net equity had reached approximately $350,000, compared with the $40,000 recorded at the beginning of the marriage.This increase was the result of both the decrease in the mortgage debt and the increase in the property value over the years. The couple had paid down about $41,000 of the mortgage during the marriage.The trial court attributed most of the increase in equity to rising property values rather than the couple's financial contributions.What the lower court decided about the marital residenceThe trial court entered a final divorce decree on February 20, 2025, awarding the residence to Allen. Meredith received $50,000, her share of the equity in the house and Allen's UPS Class A common stock.The court characterized the original $40,000 equity as Allen’s separate property. It also held that the increase in equity due to market forces was not divisible between the spouses.Using that calculation, only the $41,000 spent paying down the mortgage during marriage was marital property to be divided. But the court ignored the couple's investment of about $40,000 to complete and remodel the basement.Meredith took issue with both parts of the ruling, alleging the court erred by failing to include the equity increase from market appreciation and failing to consider the basement renovation a marital investment.Why the appeals court rejected the original property calculationThe Georgia Court of Appeals examined a legal principle known as the source of funds rule, which applies when one spouse owns a residence before marriage but marital money is subsequently invested in it.The rule requires courts to consider 3 financial elements. These include the property's equity when the couple married, the amount of marital money invested in the residence and its equity at the time of divorce.The calculation helps distinguish the original owner's separate property from the portion of the home's value that became subject to equitable division through contributions made during the marriage.The appeals court found that the trial court had incorrectly treated the entire increase in equity caused by market appreciation as Allen's separate property.It cited earlier Georgia decisions, including Hubby v. Hubby, to explain that when marital money reduces the debt secured against a residence, the other spouse may be entitled to a share of the increase in equity, including appreciation resulting indirectly from those payments.The court decided that Meredith could not be excluded from the market-driven increase simply because Allen had originally owned the property.A fresh division of the couple's marital estate orderedThe appeals court also found that the failure to include the basement renovation in the calculation was a separate error.The approximately $40,000 spent transforming the basement into a living space for Meredith's parents was undisputed evidence of marital investment in the residence. That expenditure should have been considered when determining the total amount invested in the property during the marriage. Because the lower court had omitted this contribution, it had not correctly applied the source of funds rule.It vacated the portion of the divorce decree dealing with equitable division and sent the case back to the trial court with instructions to carry out a new division consistent with its ruling.You use AI every day. articles.title: A New Mexico artist spent more than a year turning parts from a 1953 Chevy Bel Air into a 10-foot-tall, 1,200-pound jackrabbit sculpture celebrating Route 66
articles.summary: It started with a chase.
articles.body: It started with a chase. Two days before the city of Gallup asked Robert Wilson to make a sculpture for Route 66, he was running after jackrabbits on the trails of Albuquerque’s West Mesa. So, when the opportunity came, jackrabbits were the first thing that came to mind.Jackrabbits are quick, built for desert crossings and muscular; they seemed like a fitting symbol for the historic highway. In those respects, they were also similar to the old cars that once ruled the highway. At that moment, he knew he had to combine the jackrabbit and the car. That idea became Run, a giant jackrabbit sculpture made from salvaged parts of a 1953 Chevy Bel Air.Sculpture from a salvaged carWilson chose a 1953 Chevrolet Bel Air as his raw material. He cut the car into pieces with a plasma torch, a tool he had never used before. Taking a car apart was new to him, too. Then he began the slow work of welding the pieces into a new shape.The car’s lines made the job easier. The curves already looked like an animal to him. "The '53 Chevy Bel Air has curves and a kind of muscularity that I think fit with an animal like a jackrabbit," he told KOAT.The artist, who retired from medicine in 2016 to focus on art full-time, said he was thrilled to have the opportunity. "I was overjoyed," he said.A rabbit mid-hopThe finished sculpture stands just over 10 feet tall and weighs 1,280 pounds. It is roughly the size of a car, which makes sense given where it came from. The rabbit looks frozen at the moment it leaves the ground.Wilson did not sand away the signs of age on the car. Paint, wear and rust remain on the metal, giving it more character. The surfaces still carry the car’s history, allowing visitors to see the Bel Air hidden inside the animal.The artist also added a few hidden touches. The rabbit’s left eye is the car’s original speedometer, permanently set at 66 miles per hour. That number is a nod to Route 66 itself. "You always see something you didn’t see before," he told New Mexico magazine.People passing by can take a moment to observe the artwork. Study the paws, ears and legs, and you will start guessing which parts of the car became which body parts. Wilson wants people to keep looking because the sculpture rewards a second glance. "Look for parts of the paws and the ears and try to figure out what part of the car was used to make that paw, that leg," he told the station.The sculpture sits at the west end of Babe Ruth Park in Gallup. It is close to the westbound lanes of Interstate 40 at Exit 22 and faces the El Rancho Hotel, a historic landmark on the old highway. Gallup has built much of its Route 66 identity around that hotel and the road that runs past it. So, this new installation is hard to miss. The project was commissioned to mark the highway’s 100th anniversary, and the location was chosen with that in mind. Travellers passing through now have a reason to pull over.For Wilson, this work is 'recycled art'. He described Run in those terms. "RUN is meant to express the unexpected beauty found in re-used industrial materials," he said.The artwork aligns with the spirit of Route 66, where weathered signs, giant statues and quirky roadside stops have pulled drivers off the highway for decades. The latest addition, Run, joins that tradition with a sculpture made entirely from scrap.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: DAVID MARCUS: Where does the blue tsunami leave old school Dems like John Fetterman?
articles.summary: John Fetterman's moderate stance on Israel and immigration puts him at odds with the Democratic Party's ascendant progressive wing in the new Senate.
articles.body: On Tuesday night, the American people triggered a political earthquake by thrusting Democrats into power in both the House and Senate by overwhelming margins. The defeat has already left the GOP in a circular firing squad of recrimination, but Democrats, too, must now face their own party's new divisions. That’s where Pennsylvania Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., comes in front and center. Fetterman in recent years has replaced former Sens. Joe Manchin, of West Virginia, and Kyrsten Sinema, of Arizona, as the most vocal and pugnacious moderate on issues such as immigration enforcement, support for Israel and a refusal to shut down the government to achieve liberal policy wins. MAVERICK DEMOCRAT SURGES WITH REPUBLICANS AS HIS OWN PARTY TURNS ON HIM, STOKING TALK OF GOP SWITCH Fetterman's penchant for criticizing progressive shibboleths was one thing when Democrats toiled in the minority, but how will incoming Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and his leadership team deal with the Pennsylvania maverick now that they control the upper chamber? It is possible that Schumer just waits Fetterman out. The latter is up for re-election in 2028 and currently, according to surveys, is more popular with Keystone State Republicans than with Democratic voters there, making his chances of retaining the seat, at least as a Democrat, rather remote. CHUCK SCHUMER AFTER SWEEPING DEMOCRATIC MIDTERM VICTORIES: 'I'LL BE RE-ELECTED AS MAJORITY LEADER' Fetterman, it should be noted, is not the only nominally moderate Democrat facing voters in a purple state in two years. There are also Patty Murray of Washington, Maggie Hassan of New Hampshire and Catherine Cortez Masto of Nevada. But one must ask: Will they be more afraid of a general election defeat from the right or a primary ouster from the left? A year ago, Democrats had dreams of a Senate majority, but it wasn't quite the Senate majority they have wound up with. In Michigan, they expected a Haley Stevens or Mallory McMorrow, not an Abdul El-Sayed. In Maine, an Angie Craig, not a Troy Jackson. These avatars of the progressive wing of the party will be the celebrities of the next Congress. MAJORITY OF AMERICANS BROADLY REJECT SOCIALIST IDEOLOGY EVEN AS FAR LEFT SURGES TO POWER It is difficult to imagine this firebrand faction working hand in hand with a White House they flat-out accuse of fascism to pass bipartisan legislation. But just as hard-line MAGA senators have been frustrated by Senate Majority Leader John Thune's temperance on issues such as killing the filibuster, incoming leader Chuck Schumer may well wish to resist the resistance, so to speak. In fact, establishment Democrats and media pundits have been quick to remind us all that the vast majority of Democrats serving at the Capitol are not of the socialist variety, even though the party's zeitgeist and primary wins such as those in Michigan and Maine are with them. JOE MANCHIN WARNS DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ARE GAINING GROUND AS DEMOCRATS REMAIN SILENT The good news for Democratic leadership is that the scale of the victories Tuesday gives them big enough margins — 80 or so seats in the House and four to six in the Senate — that the socialists should not be able to hold legislation hostage. But that doesn't mean they have to be quiet about it. There are several issues where we can expect the ascendant far left of the Democratic Party to draw lines in the marble of the Capitol, chief among them support for Israel and funding for immigration enforcement. Schumer will likely have to bend the knee to these demands, but not John Fetterman. As Republicans delve deep into their postmortems, assigning blame for defeat, Democrats are celebrating a kind of Easter. But the question is: What exactly is this resurrected political party? Are the socialists a flying buttress to the establishment Democrats, or are they, in fact, the body of the cathedral now? Fetterman raised eyebrows at this year's GOP midterm convention in Dallas when he appeared via video to celebrate the other Pennsylvania senator, Republican Dave McCormick, leading some to believe that the sweatshirt-wearing contrarian could switch parties — something he has consistently told the media, including this columnist, that he will never do. Democrats in leadership have insisted for months that there has not been a far-left takeover of the party of Jefferson and Jackson, but rather that there is simply a big tent. Well, we know the tent is big enough for the likes of California streamer and anti-Israel firebrand Hasan Piker, but is there room in it for John Fetterman? articles.title: Social media horrified by Dave Chappelle’s sick ‘joke’ about Charlie Kirk’s murder

articles.body: Comedian Dave Chappelle said he feels "better" following the assassination of Turning Point USA (TPUSA) founder Charlie Kirk during a stand-up performance in New York City on Friday night, provoking outrage across social media. articles.title: Iran threatens to ‘rain down hell’ if US escalates war
articles.summary: President Trump warns that US forces are ‘locked and loaded’ and ready to strike, if necessary.
articles.body:
Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, has warned that Tehran will “rain down hell” if the United States resumes attacks, serving Washington with an ultimatum in an attempt to end the two countries’ eight-month war.

“Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results,” Araghchi wrote in a post on X on Sunday.

“Or choose war, and see our alert and battle-hardened warriors rain down hell,” he said.

US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that renewed strikes on Iran are “highly unlikely” if negotiations progress over Tehran’s nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

“It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement,” Trump said when asked about continued US strikes on Iran during a phone interview reported by CNN. “I would [continue], if necessary, but we hit them really hard,” he added.

Trump warned that US forces have three aircraft carriers stationed in the region “fully locked and loaded”, ready to continue strikes if need be. He also said that the US has 38 bridges in Iran’s crosshairs that US forces “can knock down in literally one hour”.

Iran’s Foreign Ministry also quoted Araghchi in an earlier statement on Sunday that said Iran would “not go easy on American targets” in the region.

Araghchi’s statements came after reports by state media that an oil tanker caught fire earlier that morning after hitting a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz , citing Iran’s navy.

The navy claimed the ship’s identification systems were turned off and it was travelling in the no-go zone of the strait.

An adviser to Iran’s commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Aerospace Force made threats that echoed those of the Iranian foreign minister and said that weapons have been “secured for years to come”.

“The armed forces are at the ready, and if the enemy makes a mistake, Iran’s response will be devastating and severe,” warned IRGC Brigadier-General Ali Belali in a statement on Telegram.

“As senior commanders of the armed forces have pointed out, we have upgraded our capabilities in the post-Ramadan War period,” Belali said.

The back-and-fourth between Iranian and US leaders comes following US midterm elections in which the Democratic Party won control of both chambers of Congress, soundly defeating Trump’s Republican Party.

Araghchi alleged that negotiations have been delayed as a result of the elections, but he awaits the path forward, Iranian state media reported.

“It will take some time for things to settle down and for the atmosphere to become conducive to the mediators resuming their visits,” the foreign minister said. “We have to wait.”

articles.title: Maya Jama steps down as host of reality TV show Love Island
articles.summary: The presenter tells fans it is "time to throw myself into something new" after recent Celebrity Traitors success.
articles.body:
Presenter Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as the host of reality TV show Love Island after three years.

The 32-year-old wrote on Instagram alongside a highlights reel of her on the programme that it was "time to throw myself into something new".

"While my own Love Island journey has come to an end, I wish the show and the team all the success in the world, I'll be cheering you lot on from the sidelines forever," the TV and radio presenter said.

Jama's announcement comes hot on the heels of an appearance as a contestant on Celebrity Traitors that won her praise and speculation in the Times that she could "get £1m per deal" thanks to her success.

Thanking fans and the production team on Love Island, she said she had an "unforgettable time" on the programme.

"I started hosting the show aged 28 and during the nine incredible series met the most wonderful humans along the way. I've loved every slow-mo walk, fire pit and live show.

But she added: "I've always believed that to truly grow, you have to take a leap every now and then."

Jama landed her biggest presenting role to date as the host of the reality TV show in 2023, taking over from Laura Whitmore.

The programme couples contestants together who then complete a range of tasks and keep swapping in the hope of meeting the love of their life.

An ITV spokesperson said: "Maya has been a fantastic and much loved host on Love Island - we thank her for everything she has brought to the show over the last three years and wish her every continued success."

Love Island is one of the most popular reality TV shows in the UK but the series has polarised viewers, with some arguing the show is misogynistic and raising concerns about the welfare of contestants.

Ofcom has previously received tens of thousands of complaints about Love Island including about alleged misogynistic and bullying behaviour by some contestants.

The watchdog has previously described the show as "emotionally charged" with "confrontational scenes" that can upset some viewers.

Jama first built her profile through radio including a role on Rinse FM, before landing a presenting role on BBC Radio 1 in 2018.

She went on to present a string of television programmes, including Channel 4's Stand Up To Cancer and ITV2's Don't Hate the Playaz, before taking over as host of BBC Three's Glow Up: Britain's Next Make-Up Star in 2021.

The presenter was recently watched by millions in the Celebrity Traitors final, and competed as a traitor alongside actor Richard E Grant, Youtuber King Kenny and comedian James Acaster during the series.

One commentator at the time said that, despite not winning the show, she had emerged as a winner of sorts as she was able to portray herself as "less like the presenter of Love Island and more like a genuinely versatile television star".

Her Celebrity Traitors appearance came after she made her acting debut in the second series of Guy Ritchie's Netflix drama The Gentlemen alongside Theo James and Kaya Scodelario.

Jama had auditioned for the cult Channel 4 series Skins, set in her hometown of Bristol, when she was 15, reaching the final stage for a role in the show that launched the careers of actors Daniel Kaluuya and Dev Patel.

She moved to London when she was 16 to pursue a career in the entertainment industry.

She began presenting a weekly music video countdown for production company JumpOff TV before joining MTV in 2014 as a presenter on The Wrap Up.

Jama became the youngest person to host the MOBO Awards, alongside Marvin Humes, in 2017.

articles.title: In 2024, two Wisconsin teens launched a food drive at their high school; by 2026, Meals Matter had expanded to over 35 chapters and 3,500 volunteers, collecting more than $550,000 in cash and food donations
articles.summary: Noah Duckett and Wyatt Ehrhardt started their food drive in 2024, the same year they finished high school.
articles.body: Noah Duckett and Wyatt Ehrhardt started their food drive in 2024, the same year they finished high school. Two years later, the initiative they began in a Wisconsin town has grown into a national network and earned one of the most prestigious youth honours in the world. Duckett and Ehrhardt, both now college sophomores, have received The Diana Award for co-founding Meals Matter, a student-led non-profit that fights food insecurity.Starting small in MiddletonThe high school students initially started the food drive on a much smaller scale. The idea was simple: collect food from neighbours and get it to families who needed it. Their first drives filled bags and boxes, and the work continued long after the first month. They initially called it Middleton Meals Matter.At the time, they wanted to do something bigger than a school project but weren't sure what. Clothing and food were both options. They chose food. Food insecurity in Wisconsin had reached a 30-year high, and they wanted to do something about it.In the initial months, they organised food drives and handed the collected items to WayForward Resources, a local food pantry that stored and distributed the donations. Grocery stores became regular partners. They later added themed events such as Halloween for Hunger and Summer Stock-Up. These events gave students a reason to show up again and again.As the drives became popular, students from other schools also showed interest. They wanted to know how to run their own drives. So Duckett and Ehrhardt built a structure to help new students get involved and expand the programme. Under their leadership, the non-profit has raised more than $550,000 through monetary and food donations and grown to more than 35 high school chapters, with over 3,500 young volunteers supporting chapters across the United States and South Korea.The students also met with state lawmakers to discuss policy options for fighting food insecurity. Members learned to speak in public, presenting to students and community groups about why hunger needs attention. The group later became a 501(c)(3) non-profit organisation.RecognitionNoah Duckett and Wyatt Ehrhardt have also received recognition for their work. They won the 2026 William R. Simms Award for Outstanding Youth in Philanthropy. They have now received The Diana Award, which recognises young people who tackle pressing problems in their communities.“Winning the Diana Award means a lot to me. Meals Matter began as a local effort to help our neighbours in Middleton, and today it’s a national organisation helping feed families in communities across the country and overseas,” Ehrhardt said. “This award belongs just as much to our volunteers and to the community members who show up at our food drives and events to help fight food insecurity. I hope this shows other students that you don’t have to wait until you’re older to lead. You just need to decide to act and trust that your community will have your back. Ours always has.”Duckett said the win was “one of the biggest honours” of his life. “When we held that first food drive in Middleton, I never imagined it would turn into a national network of more than 35 chapters, all led by students who saw hunger in their communities and refused to look away. Every meal packed and every chapter launched came from young people who believed they could make a difference, and this award belongs to all of them. It shows what one idea can become when people commit to it. Representing Wisconsin, and especially Middleton, means everything to me. This is where Meals Matter started, and I hope every student here knows that the next big idea could be theirs.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Massive Amsterdam march challenges Dutch government's response to Israel's war in Gaza
articles.summary: More than 200,000 people took part in a march through Amsterdam on Sunday, calling on the Dutch government to take stronger action against Israel over its
articles.body: More than 200,000 people took part in a march through Amsterdam on Sunday, calling on the Dutch government to take stronger action against Israel over its military campaign in Gaza, according to the Dutch branch of Amnesty International, one of the organisers.Many protesters wore red as they joined the demonstration, known as the ‘Red Line’ march, demanding tighter trade restrictions on Israel, an end to arms sales and measures against what organisers described as genocide in Gaza.The organisers said the Dutch government should impose stricter trade sanctions and halt all weapons exports to Israel. Amnesty International Netherlands said in an online post that more than 200,000 people had participated in the demonstration. The Associated Press (AP) also reported on the march.Protesters criticised the government's response to the conflict, with demonstrators arguing that diplomatic pressure and existing restrictions had not gone far enough.“What is happening there is inhumane,” Mike van Dongen said as he walked among the demonstrators.He also questioned the government's approach, saying: “As far as I'm concerned, they are doing nothing. They don't dare take any serious steps.”The march moved along a major Amsterdam street that was closed to traffic for the demonstration. A man standing at a bus stop used a loudspeaker to lead chants of “Free, free Palestine!”, with many protesters repeating the slogan as they passed.The demonstration comes amid continuing disagreement over Israel's military campaign in Gaza, launched after Hamas-led militants attacked southern Israel on October 7, 2023, killing around 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages, according to the figures cited in the report.Israel rejects allegations that it is committing genocide. Its military offensive has killed tens of thousands of Palestinians and devastated large parts of Gaza.According to Gaza's Health Ministry, more than 1,550 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces since a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas began in October 2025. The ministry, which operates under the Hamas-run administration, does not distinguish between civilian and militant deaths, but says women and children account for roughly half of those killed.The conflict has also strained relations between the Netherlands and Israel. The Dutch government has introduced an import ban on products from Israeli settlements, which it considers illegal under international law, prompting a diplomatic dispute with Israel.Prime Minister Rob Jetten defended his administration's approach at a press conference on Friday, saying: “Every single day and every single week, we do what we can to alleviate the terrible situation there.”He said the government was “exerting greater political and diplomatic pressure" on Israel to honour its commitments on Gaza, while also increasing pressure on Hamas and other groups over actions that threaten Israeli civilians.You use AI every day. articles.title: Independent wrestling's heart still beating even as social media begins to write its obituary
articles.summary: Ben Bishop and Killer Kross dismiss claims that independent wrestling is dead after Fight Factory's No Thanks Given drew hundreds in New Jersey.
articles.body: The pro wrestling conversation on social media usually ranges from hotly contested debates between which company is better, WWE or AEW, fans complaining about the way their favorite wrestler is booked or there being too many commercials on TV. OK, maybe the last one is just me tweeting into the void. Regardless, there was a lot of chatter online about independent wrestling being "dead." The noise around the notion appeared to spark when Produce Wrestling and Absolute Intense Wrestling (AIW) announced hiatuses for different reasons for the end of the year. For what it’s worth, Produce already has a show booked for Feb. 25. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE OutKick Dropkick has put the spotlight on several independent shows this year with a few different promotions, including Pandemonium Pro Wrestling, Awesome Championship Wrestling, Produce Wrestling, Gamechanger Wrestling, Fight Factory Wrestling and others. So, as social media wrote an obituary for the indies, OutKick Dropkick made its way to Middletown, New Jersey, on Friday night to take in Fight Factory’s No Thanks Given and to see whether the vibes would be more of a concert or a wake. It didn’t disappoint. Ben Bishop, who made a surprise appearance at Total Nonstop Action Wrestling’s (TNA) Bound for Glory pay-per-view assembled a team for an elimination eight-person tag team match against MADE. Richard Holliday, Jack Vaughn and Madisyn Maxwell went up against Made. Kristin Blaze then defeated Rachel Ley in a preview of what women’s wrestling may look like in the future. Even WWE Hall of Famer Arn Anderson showed up to support his sons as they took on Sent 2 Salute. The main event featured a no holds barred match between TNA star KC Navarro and Steve Gibki for the latter’s openweight championship. The match ended with Gibki spearing Navarro through a table and putting his opponent in the Hell Hammer for the win. The show was held at the Middletown Sports Complex, which is not a large venue by any means. But pro wrestling fans still showed up to fill the available seats. Most lasted through the chilly conditions since the event took place on a literal ice rink, which is also the home of the North American Hockey League’s New Jersey Titans. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE There certainly was no funeral for independent wrestling. In fact, attendees were actively engaged in the sport that was happening in and outside of the ring. OutKick Dropkick asked Bishop whether he believed the indies were dead. "I mean, look at it, look at it here. In Middletown, New Jersey, on a Friday night, you could be doing anything," Bishop said. "We're close to (New York City). There's a ton of things you can do. We got about 300, almost 400-plus here in Middletown, New Jersey, here at Fight Factory. You can thank me for the house. So yeah, this whole notion, indies are dead, all that stuff, it's just words, it's just noise. It comes up every few months. Everyone wants to pretend that they think that when they were wrestling on the indies, it was so much better. It is what it is. Things evolve, things change. I believe that indie wrestling is alive and well." Bishop is right. Anyone who was in the facility on Friday night could have been doing anything else. WWE’s "Friday Night SmackDown" was on TV, "World of Warcraft’s" new game just dropped, there was basketball and hockey going on at the same time. And maybe you don’t know who Ben Bishop is. Maybe you didn’t see his "curtain call" with Holliday, Vaughn and Tommy Invincible at War on the Shore 3 that had social media talking over the summer. And all of that is OK. OutKick Dropkick asked Killer Kross his thoughts about the same notion. Kross works for a big-time company in Major League Wrestling, which has multiple media rights deals and partnerships with CMLL and New Japan Pro-Wrestling. However, he’s gone on his own tours in the U.S. and abroad for promotions big and small. Kross said he wasn’t necessarily plugged into the conversation but suggested that the attendance at independent events undercut the notion that independent wrestling is dying. "These are people who don't attend indies that are saying that, and I don't even think they're saying it to be malicious. I think they're just innocently saying it because You know, when, when you're a young adult and you have a very busy life, if you're not paying attention to something, or like you're not paying attention to the big main thing that everybody's paying attention to, then you innocently will think that it's not important cause it doesn't have your attention. "But when you go to an independent show where there's 2,000-3000 people there, That kind of speaks for itself. I don't get involved with neurotic conversations online. You know what I mean? And it's OK. Anyone can express their opinion about anything they want. I don't get hung up on that, but like … I don't know, I'm not emotionally prone to these types of conversations. Some people are like, ‘Well, I gotta drop everything I'm doing and respond.’ I'm like, I don't have the time. I don't have the time." articles.title: Week 10 AP Poll sees Georgia rightfully take over top spot while voters continue to award USC for no reason
articles.summary: Georgia jumped to No. 1 after dismantling Ole Miss 42-7, while the Alabama-Tennessee ranking debate and USC's puzzling rise stir controversy.
articles.body: Week 10 had the potential to be one of the more chaotic and disruptive weekends of the college football season, with seven ranked-on-ranked matchups. Naturally, five of those seven matchups were won by the favorite, and instead of a weekend resulting in chaos, it was a weekend of teams making statements. It's always the loaded slates that hardly ever meet expectations, and the weekends you least expect that deliver the goods. No team sent a stronger statement on Saturday than the Georgia Bulldogs with their 42-7 dismantling of Ole Miss on the road, and they were rewarded with the No. 1 being added next to their name. The Dawgs and Rebels each threw for 186 yards in the game, but all was not equal on the ground, as Georgia dominated both lines of scrimmage and picked up 295 rushing yards compared to Ole Miss' 66 yards on the ground. Week 10 AP Top 25 Poll Perhaps the biggest stunner from Week 10 is that AP voters finally got things right, at least for the most part. Yes, they caught a break with the mostly chalk results and a lack of difficult decisions to make, but for as much as we love to pile it on when the poll is a disaster, we have to tip our cap on the rare occasion that the poll makes a lot of sense. Georgia may have a loss, unlike the two unbeatens of Utah and UCLA, but there is no reality where someone could watch what the Bulldogs did to Ole Miss on Saturday night and not tab them as the No. 1 team in the country. Notre Dame had to get rewarded in some fashion If anyone wants to waste energy arguing about how UCLA and Utah should both be ranked ahead of one-loss Notre Dame, they can have at it. Just like there isn't a world where Georgia shouldn't be ranked No. 1, there also isn't a world where voters were going to put both Utah and UCLA ahead of the Fighting Irish after they knocked off Miami. Notre Dame couldn't stay put at No. 4 after beating the team that the same voters had ranked No. 1 in the country one week ago. And no, it does not matter that Miami's best player, Malachi Toney, did not play. ALABAMA FINALLY PUTS IT ALL TOGETHER, DOMINATES LSU AND LEAVES LANE KIFFIN STARING AT $40 MILLION CFP DISASTER The Tennessee-Alabama conundrum Is Alabama being ranked No. 7 and Tennessee being ranked No. 9 that big of a deal? No, none of this is with the College Football Playoff Rankings taking all precedence, but Vols fans have every right to be frustrated with the Tide being ranked ahead of them. Alabama and Tennessee are both 7-2 on the season, and with the Volunteers beating the Crimson Tide by 16 points earlier this season, the 'tiebreaker' should go Tennessee's way. On top of that, Tennessee dominated then No. 8 Kentucky 34-6 in Week 10. NO 3 UTAH REMAINS UNDEFEATED WITH THRILLING WIN OVER NO 9 BYU BEHIND HEISMAN FINALIST DEVON DAMPIER'S EPIC DAY THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Alabama going to Baton Rouge and beating up on then No. 15 LSU on Saturday can't and shouldn't be ignored, but with Tennessee winning the head-to-head and having the more impressive win on paper, it doesn't make much sense to have the Vols ranked behind the Tide this week. Tennessee fans can also point a (small) finger at Texas in this situation as well. The Longhorns beat Tennessee in Knoxville, hence their ranking ahead of the Vols, and with voters having to rank these teams somewhere, Texas really not being able to fall anywhere other than No. 8 adds another wrinkle to the mess. If we got into all the resumes, hypotheticals, and head-to-head matchups, we'd be here all day. USC is still getting way too much respect We pointed out last week that the Trojans were getting way too much love from the voters, moving up to the No. 18 spot after knocking off what we now know is a very mediocre Ohio State team. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER This week, USC was on a bye, and its signature win against the Buckeyes looks even worse with Ohio State losing to Oregon, yet the Trojans moved up three spots to No. 15 by simply not playing. I'd say make it make sense, but it doesn't. USC has one notable win against a now three-loss Buckeyes team and losses to Oregon and Wisconsin. That is not the resume of a Top 15 team in the country. Actual reality will fall into place in Week 11 when the Trojans travel to Bloomington to take on No. 6 Indiana in a monster matchup.

articles.body: Prince George’s County and the Boris L. Henson Foundation, founded by actress and mental health advocate Taraji P. Henson, are partnering on a $30 million Healing Arts Integrative Wellness Hub in Temple Hills, Maryland. According to the Prince George’s County Council, the county will renovate the Temple Hills Community Centre into a facility combining creative arts, wellness practices and evidence-based mental health services. The foundation will oversee programming, including hip hop therapy, arts and yoga, and residents will be able to use the centre free of charge. The council says the funding has been moved from the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission’s budget, with construction expected to begin in 2026.How will Henson's foundation support mental health in MarylandThe council says the Boris L. Youth Symposium held in May. The release lists hip hop therapy, arts and yoga among them.The release also says the centre will focus on combating social isolation among senior citizens. County Executive Aisha Braveboy is quoted as saying it is important to have "a mental health and wellness facility here in the County." According to the release, she said families sometimes need a mental health professional to help them process life's challenges, stress and anxiety, and that the facility can give residents a place and the confidence to seek help and healing.How will the Maryland wellness hub provide free services to residentsResidents will be able to use the centre free of charge. The release also says Prince George's County has moved $30 million from the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission's budget for the initiative.According to the council, construction is expected to begin in 2026. The release credits the partnership to the Boris L. Henson Foundation, the Prince George's County Government, the County Council and the Park and Planning Commission. It names Council Chair Edward Burroughs III and Commission Chairman Darryl Barnes among those involved.Prince George's County say it needs a new mental health and wellness hubIn the release, Council Chair Edward Burroughs III says the council must act against rising stress, trauma and hopelessness in communities. He links this to the effects of federal-level decisions on the economy and on residents. He says the council feels a responsibility and a duty to respond.Burroughs also thanks the Boris L. articles.summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai took to Instagram to wish everyone a Happy Diwali, sharing a photo of a vibrant rangoli created at the company's India office.
articles.body: Google CEO Sundar Pichai took to Instagram to wish everyone a Happy Diwali, sharing a photo of a vibrant rangoli created at the company's India office. “Sending lots of light and love to everyone celebrating Diwali 💛,” Pichai wrote in his post. Highlighting the festive setup, he added, “Made with lots of colors, flowers and diyas, this rangoli comes from our celebrations at @GoogleIndia 🪔.”The photo shows a vibrant, traditional Diwali rangoli featuring the Google logo at its centre. The rangoli is circular and crafted on a dark floor using coloured powders and intricate floral patterns. At the centre there is the iconic multi-colored Google “G” logo, surrounded by concentric layers of teal, white and yellow floral motifs. The entire artwork is lined with a thick, circular border of bright orange marigold flowers. On the outer perimeter, the rangoli is illuminated by numerous lit earthen lamps (diyas), adding a warm, festive glow to the celebration.Google’s Diwali Doodle 2026Alongside Pichai's post, Google has rolled out an interactive surprise on its search platform to celebrate the festival, with Search marking Diwali with interactive Lakshmi Puja feature.When users search for “Diwali,” an ornate wooden mandir pops up on the right side of the results page, showing Goddess Lakshmi seated on a golden platform. Clicking on the golden birds and decorative elements around the temple triggers animations that add more sweets, flowers and offerings, eventually leading to a fireworks display.The feature centers on Lakshmi Puja, the worship ritual performed on Diwali night. The temple is designed with multiple levels, and has stepped levels, domes, golden bells, lit diyas and trays of offerings, all set in swirling floral patterns of orange, yellow and black.A look back at Pichai’s viral ‘Google Barfi’ postPichai’s festive social media posts have become something of a tradition. articles.body: Newly released 911 calls capture the frantic aftermath of an alligator attack that left a Florida woman with severe injuries, according to reports. The attack occurred as Dina Spann, 58, was swimming with a group in Florida's Silver River near Ray Wayside Park in Marion County over the summer. Spann survived the attack but lost her right arm below the elbow and part of a finger on her left hand. FLORIDA DAD MAKES FINAL FACETIME CALL TO WIFE BEFORE DYING IN FLASH FLOOD Audio of two 911 calls obtained by The New York Post captured the frantic moments after the attack, including witnesses describing Spann's severe injuries. "Somebody got bit by an alligator, I think her arm got bit — it’s dangling off," one woman said in the call, the Post said. "She lost half an arm." In another 911 call, a woman can be heard screaming and crying as a man tells the dispatcher they are on the Silver River. "Her arm is gone," the second 911 caller said. MOM OF 2 WHO DIED RESCUING SONS DURING BAHAMAS SNORKELING TRIP IS IDENTIFIED Fox News Digital reported on the August incident earlier this year. At the time, Spann's son, Zach Guerrina, told the Post his mother was trying to hold the alligator's jaws open so she could escape. "It had her, but she said she was trying to make sure it didn’t get to her legs," he said. Other eyewitnesses shared their accounts of the incident.
